title: Error Handling, Resilience and Cost Control
why: Every question is one or more HTTP calls to Gemini, and Gemini sometimes fails: 429, 503, a timeout. Right now the user sees a 500 when that happens. Today we sort the errors (which ones we retry and which we don't), add retry and timeout with one package, a fallback model, and write the tokens of every call to the database, so we know what today cost. Without this an AI feature doesn't make it to production.
outcomes: You'll sort an error as transient, permanent or a content error, and explain which ones retry helps with
You'll add retry, timeout and a circuit breaker to an HttpClient with `AddStandardResilienceHandler`, give that client to Google.GenAI and turn off its own retry
You'll write a `FallbackChatClient` that calls a fallback model on a transient error
You'll write the tokens of every call to the database (`IServiceScopeFactory`) and calculate the day's cost

review.q: Which error does retry help with, and which doesn't it? One example each.
review.a: Transient — 429, 500/503, timeout, the network: trying again helps · permanent — 400, 401, 403, 404: the same request brings the same error · content (length, bad JSON) — in code

review.q: Why don't we retry 10 times right away? What are backoff and jitter?
review.a: We'd send an overloaded service even more requests · backoff — a growing pause (2→4→8 s) · jitter — a random part, so many clients don't retry at the same time · on a 429 — Retry-After

review.q: Why do we turn off Google.GenAI's own retry?
review.a: Retry must be in one place · two nested retries = 4 × 4 = 16 attempts and minutes of waiting · `HttpRetryOptions { Attempts = 1 }` + our HttpClient through `ClientOptions.HttpClientFactory`

review.q: Where does `FallbackChatClient` stand in the pipeline, and which errors does it catch?
review.a: Innermost (the last `.Use`) — every request of the tool loop gets its own fallback · only transient ones: ApiException 429/5xx, the network, a timeout · `catch … when`

review.q: Why does TokenCounter get the DbContext through `IServiceScopeFactory` to write to the database?
review.a: The pipeline is a Singleton, the DbContext is Scoped · injecting it directly = a captive dependency · the layer creates its own scope every time

quiz.q: Gemini returned a 503. What does it mean and what do we do?
options: A bug in our code — let's fix it
Gemini is temporarily overloaded — let's try again a bit later
The key ran out — let's get a new one
quiz.explain: 503 — a transient error: retry, and if that doesn't work — a fallback model.

quiz.q: On which error should we **not** try again?
quiz.explain: 401 is permanent: the same key brings the same error. Retry only on transient ones.

quiz.q: An answer arrived (200), but FinishReason = length and the JSON is cut off. Which group is this?
options: Content — we check it in code (MaxOutputTokens, TryGetResult)
quiz.explain: At the HTTP level everything's fine — our code checks the content of the answer.

options: A growing pause between retries: 2 → 4 → 8 seconds
quiz.explain: The overloaded service gets time to catch its breath. Jitter adds a random part to the pause.

quiz.q: What does a circuit breaker do?
options: After many failures it temporarily stops the calls and returns an error right away
quiz.explain: The service rests, the user doesn't wait for nothing.

quiz.q: Why do we raise `AttemptTimeout` from 10 seconds to 40?
options: Gemini thinks and writes long answers — 10 seconds sometimes isn't enough, and a normal answer would “fail”
The number of retries will grow
quiz.explain: The default time is meant for fast APIs. An LLM needs more.

quiz.q: What happens if we don't turn off Google.GenAI's retry and add resilience too?
options: Nothing — they don't touch each other
The retries nest: many more attempts and much more waiting for one question

quiz.q: With `ChaosHandler`: two 503s and then a 200. What does the user see?
options: An ordinary answer, a little late (~6 seconds)
quiz.explain: The retry happens inside the HttpClient — the Controller and the user never saw the error.

quiz.q: Why doesn't `FallbackChatClient` kick in on a 401?
options: `IsTransient` treats 401 as permanent: the fallback model uses the same key and would bring the same error
The fallback only works with streaming
quiz.explain: The fallback only on a transient error: 429, 5xx, the network, a timeout.

quiz.q: In a Singleton layer, why do we get `DataContext` through `IServiceScopeFactory`?
options: The pipeline is a Singleton, the DbContext Scoped; injecting it directly would share one DbContext across every request
A DbContext works in a Singleton too
EF Core requires it for migrations
quiz.explain: The layer creates its own scope every time and takes the DbContext from it.

summary: Errors: **transient** (429, 5xx, timeout — retry helps), **permanent** (400, 401, 403, 404 — no), **content** (length, bad JSON, a tool error — in code).
A proper retry: **backoff + jitter**, `Retry-After`, a **timeout** per attempt, a **circuit breaker**. `AddStandardResilienceHandler` — on the HttpClient, with times raised for an LLM.
Google.GenAI uses our HttpClient (`ClientOptions.HttpClientFactory`), its retry is turned off (`Attempts = 1`): retry in **one** place.
**`FallbackChatClient`** — a fallback model on a transient error; the innermost layer of the pipeline; `catch … when`.
Tokens **in the database** (`AiUsage`): `IServiceScopeFactory`, because the pipeline is a Singleton; thinking tokens are added to the output; cost = tokens × price.
